questions.stem: A clinician's note measures a rectangular wound 8 cm by 5 cm; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Rectangle area is length times width. Eight times 5 equals 40 square centimeters. The tempting error is adding dimensions.

questions.learningObjective: Interpret unit square count as area
questions.stem: A clinician's note counts 18 unit squares covering a region; what area does it represent?

options.text: It confuses area with length units.
The covered region area is 18 square units.
It confuses area with volume units.
It doubles the counted squares.

questions.explanation: Each unit square has area 1 square unit, so 18 squares represent 18 square units. Option A uses length, C uses volume, and D doubles the count.

questions.stem: A clinician's note describes a parallelogram with base 7 cm and perpendicular height 4 cm; which expression gives area?

options.text: It uses side length instead of height.
It squares base incorrectly.
Area equals base times perpendicular height.
It adds dimensions instead of multiplying.

questions.explanation: Parallelogram area is base times perpendicular height. Option A uses side length, B squares base, and D adds dimensions. Only C is correct.

questions.stem: A clinician's note diagram shows a trapezoid with bases 6 and 10 cm and height 4 cm; which expression gives area?

options.text: It multiplies bases and height directly.
It adds dimensions instead of multiplying.
It omits height and one half.
The area equals one half times 16 times 4.

questions.explanation: Trapezoid area is one half times 6 plus 10 times 4, so one half times 16 times 4 is correct. Options A, B, and C describe common errors.

questions.learningObjective: Detect an error in kite area
questions.stem: A clinician's note computes kite area as product of diagonals for diagonals 6 and 8 cm; what error is present?

options.text: It omits the division by two.
It adds diagonals instead of multiplying.
It squares diagonals incorrectly.
It uses wrong kite formula.

questions.explanation: Kite area is one half product of diagonals, so omitting division by two is the error. Options B, C, and D describe different mistakes.

questions.stem: A clinician's note has a triangular bandage with base 10 cm height 6 cm; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Triangle area is one half base times height. One half of 10 times 6 equals 30 square centimeters. The tempting error is omitting one half.

questions.learningObjective: Compute composite area of rectangle and triangle
questions.stem: A clinician's note measures composite area as rectangle 8 by 5 plus triangle base 8 height 3; find total area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Rectangle area is 40 and triangle area is 12, so total area is 52 square centimeters. The tempting error is subtracting the triangle.

questions.topic: Composite area with a curved cut
questions.stem: A clinician's note has a rectangle 10 by 6 cm with a semicircle of radius 2 cm cut out; find remaining area in square centimeters using pi = 3.14.
questions.explanation: Rectangle area is 60 and semicircle area is 6.28, so remaining area is 53.72 square centimeters. The tempting error is subtracting a full circle.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize that different shapes can have equal areas
questions.stem: A clinician's note asks which shapes can have equal areas; what is correct?

options.text: Different shapes can have equal areas too.
Only congruent shapes have equal areas.
Area depends only on perimeter.
Equal areas require equal side lengths.
options.misconception: requires equal sides for equal area

questions.explanation: Different shapes can have equal areas when their dimensions produce the same value. Option B confuses congruence, C links area to perimeter, and D requires equal sides.

questions.stem: A clinician's note measures a rectangle 9 cm by 4 cm; which expression gives area?

options.text: It adds dimensions instead of multiplying.
The rectangle area equals 9 times 4 square cm.
It squares length incorrectly.
It squares width incorrectly.

questions.explanation: Rectangle area is length times width, so 9 times 4 is correct. Option A adds, C squares length, and D squares width.

questions.learningObjective: Compute area from a square grid
questions.stem: A clinician's note diagram shows a 4 by 5 grid of unit squares; which area results?

options.text: It adds dimensions instead of multiplying.
It confuses area with length units.
The total grid area is 20 square units total.
It doubles the counted squares.

questions.explanation: A 4 by 5 grid contains 20 unit squares, so area is 20 square units. Options A, B, and D describe common errors.

questions.learningObjective: Detect an error in parallelogram area
questions.stem: A clinician's note computes parallelogram area as base times side for base 7 height 3; what error is present?

options.text: It adds dimensions instead of multiplying.
It squares base incorrectly.
It applies triangle factor.
It should multiply base by perpendicular height.

questions.explanation: Parallelogram area uses perpendicular height, not side length. Option D states the correct operation. Options A, B, and C describe unrelated mistakes.

questions.stem: A clinician's note has trapezoid bases 5 and 9 cm height 4 cm; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Trapezoid area is one half times 5 plus 9 times 4, or 28 square centimeters. The tempting error is multiplying bases directly.

questions.stem: A clinician's note measures kite diagonals 10 and 6 cm; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Kite area is one half product of diagonals. One half of 10 times 6 equals 30 square centimeters. The tempting error is omitting one half.

questions.stem: A clinician's note measures triangular wound base 12 cm height 5 cm; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Triangle area is one half base times height. One half of 12 times 5 equals 30 square centimeters. The tempting error is omitting one half.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the operation for composite area
questions.stem: A clinician's note finds composite area; what is the correct approach?

options.text: It ignores smaller component areas.
It subtracts instead of adding.
It multiplies component areas.
Add the non-overlapping component areas.

questions.explanation: Composite area is the sum of non-overlapping component areas. Option A ignores parts, B subtracts, and C multiplies. Only D is correct.

questions.topic: Composite area with a curved cut
questions.learningObjective: Select remaining area after semicircular cut
questions.stem: A clinician's note has a rectangle 12 by 8 cm with a semicircle radius 3 cm cut out; which expression gives remaining area using pi = 3.14?

options.text: 12 times 8 minus one half pi 3 squared.
It adds cutout instead of subtracting.
It adds dimensions and uses full circle.
options.misconception: adds dimensions and uses full circle

options.text: It subtracts full circle not semicircle.

questions.explanation: Remaining area is rectangle area minus semicircle area, so 12 times 8 minus one half pi 3 squared is correct. Options B, C, and D describe errors.

questions.learningObjective: Compare areas of a square and triangle
questions.stem: A clinician's note diagram shows a 4 by 4 square and a triangle base 8 height 4; which statement about areas is true?

options.text: The square area is larger.
The two shapes have equal areas in this case.
The triangle area is larger.
Areas cannot be compared.

questions.explanation: The square area is 16 and the triangle area is one half of 8 times 4, or 16, so they are equal. Options A and C assume one is larger, and D is unnecessary.

questions.learningObjective: Detect an error in rectangle area
questions.stem: A clinician's note computes rectangle area as length plus width for 6 and 4 cm; what error is present?

options.text: It applies triangle factor.
It squares length incorrectly.
It should multiply length by width instead.
It adds a third dimension.

questions.explanation: Rectangle area is length times width, so multiplication is needed instead of addition. Options A, B, and D describe unrelated mistakes.

questions.learningObjective: Compute area from unit square count
questions.stem: A clinician's note counts 24 unit squares in a 6 by 4 rectangle; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: The 6 by 4 rectangle contains 24 unit squares, so its area is 24 square centimeters. The tempting error is adding dimensions.

questions.stem: A clinician's note measures parallelogram base 9 cm perpendicular height 5 cm; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Parallelogram area is base times perpendicular height. Nine times 5 equals 45 square centimeters. The tempting error is using side length.

questions.stem: A clinician's note measures trapezoid bases 8 and 12 cm height 5 cm; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Trapezoid area is one half times 8 plus 12 times 5, or 50 square centimeters. The tempting error is multiplying bases directly.

questions.stem: A clinician's note asks why kite area uses diagonals; what is correct?

options.text: It links equal sides to diagonal formula.
options.misconception: links equal sides to diagonal formula

options.text: It incorrectly links perimeter to area.
Because diagonals are perpendicular and determine area.
It claims formula due to missing data.
options.misconception: claims formula due to missing data

questions.explanation: Kite area is one half product of perpendicular diagonals, so the diagonals determine the area. Options A, B, and D give incorrect reasons.

questions.stem: A clinician's note describes triangle base 10 cm height 4 cm; which expression gives area?

options.text: It omits the one-half factor.
It adds dimensions instead of multiplying.
It squares base incorrectly.
The area equals one half times 10 times 4.

questions.explanation: Triangle area is one half base times height, so one half times 10 times 4 is correct. Options A, B, and C describe common errors.

questions.learningObjective: Detect double counting in composite area
questions.stem: A clinician's note adds component areas but counts an overlapping region twice; what error is present?

options.text: Overlapping region should be subtracted once.
It adds overlap again.
It accepts double counting.
It subtracts all areas.

questions.explanation: Overlapping area should be subtracted once to avoid double counting. Options B, C, and D describe other mistakes.

questions.stem: A clinician's note has rectangle 9 by 6 cm with semicircle radius 2 cm cut out; find remaining area in square centimeters using pi = 3.14.
questions.explanation: Rectangle area is 54 and semicircle area is 6.28, so remaining area is 47.72 square centimeters. The tempting error is subtracting a full circle.

questions.learningObjective: Find square side with equal area to triangle
questions.stem: A clinician's note asks what side length of a square gives same area as triangle base 8 height 8; find side in centimeters.
questions.explanation: Triangle area is 32, so square side is square root of 32, or 5.66 centimeters. The tempting error is using 8 as the side.
questions.hint: Take square root of triangle area.

questions.stem: A clinician's note measures rectangular dressing 12 cm by 7 cm; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Rectangle area is length times width. Twelve times 7 equals 84 square centimeters. The tempting error is adding dimensions.

questions.learningObjective: Express area from unit square count
questions.stem: A clinician's note counts 10 unit squares; how can area be expressed?

options.text: The area is 10 square units total.
It confuses area with length units.
It confuses area with volume units.
It doubles the square count.

questions.explanation: Ten unit squares represent 10 square units. Option B uses length, C uses volume, and D doubles the count.

options.text: It multiplies bases and height directly.
It adds dimensions instead of multiplying.
The area equals one half times 12 times 6.
It omits height and one half.

questions.explanation: Trapezoid area is one half times 4 plus 8 times 6, so C is correct. Options A, B, and D describe common errors.

questions.stem: A clinician's note computes kite area as product of diagonals for diagonals 5 and 10 cm; what error is present?

options.text: It adds diagonals instead of multiplying.
It squares diagonals incorrectly.
It accepts incorrect area.
The area should divide by 2.

questions.explanation: Kite area is one half product of diagonals, so division by 2 is needed. Option D states this. Options A, B, and C describe other mistakes.

questions.stem: A clinician's note has triangle base 14 cm height 5 cm; find area in square centimeters.

questions.stem: A clinician's note has a square 8 by 8 cm with a quarter circle radius 4 cm cut out; find remaining area in square centimeters using pi = 3.14.
questions.explanation: Square area is 64 and quarter circle area is 12.56, so remaining area is 51.44 square centimeters. The tempting error is subtracting a full circle.

questions.learningObjective: Compare areas of a square and triangle
questions.stem: A clinician's note asks whether a 6 by 6 square and a triangle base 12 height 6 have equal areas; what is true?

options.text: The square area is larger.
The triangle area is larger.
Areas cannot be compared.
The two shapes have equal areas in this case.

questions.explanation: Square area is 36 and triangle area is one half of 12 times 6, or 36, so they are equal. Options A and B assume one is larger, and C is unnecessary.

questions.learningObjective: Determine effect of scaling on rectangle area
questions.stem: A clinician's note asks what happens to rectangle area if length doubles and width halves; what is correct?

options.text: The rectangle area stays the same here.
Area doubles.
Area halves.
Area quadruples.

questions.explanation: Doubling length and halving width multiplies area by 2 times 1/2, or 1, so area stays the same. Options B, C, and D misapply the scale factors.

questions.learningObjective: Compute area from unit square count
questions.stem: A clinician's note counts 15 unit squares in an L-shaped region; which area results?

options.text: It confuses area with length units.
The area is 15 square units total.
It doubles the square count.
It confuses area with volume units.

questions.explanation: Fifteen unit squares represent 15 square units. Option A uses length, C doubles the count, and D uses volume.

options.text: It uses side length instead of height.
It adds dimensions instead of multiplying.
Area equals base times perpendicular height.
It squares base incorrectly.

questions.explanation: Parallelogram area is base times perpendicular height, so C is correct. Option A uses side length, B adds dimensions, and D squares base.

questions.learningObjective: Detect an error in trapezoid area
questions.stem: A clinician's note computes trapezoid area as base1 times base2 times height for bases 4 and 6 height 5; what error is present?

options.text: It adds bases without averaging.
It squares bases incorrectly.
It accepts incorrect area formula.
The two bases should be averaged first.

questions.explanation: Trapezoid area requires averaging the bases before multiplying by height. Option D states this. Options A, B, and C describe other mistakes.

questions.stem: A clinician's note measures kite diagonals 8 and 12 cm; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Kite area is one half product of diagonals. One half of 8 times 12 equals 48 square centimeters. The tempting error is omitting one half.

questions.explanation: Rectangle area is 30 and triangle area is 12, so total area is 42 square centimeters. The tempting error is subtracting the triangle.

questions.topic: Composite area with a curved cut
questions.stem: A clinician's note removes a semicircle from a rectangle; what adjustment is needed?

options.text: It adds cutout instead of subtracting.
It ignores curved cut area.
It subtracts full circle not semicircle.
The semicircle area must be subtracted from rectangle.

questions.explanation: The remaining area is rectangle area minus semicircle area. Option D states this. Options A, B, and C describe errors.

questions.stem: A clinician's note asks which pair can have equal areas; which is true?

options.text: A 4 by 4 square and an 8 by 2 rectangle.
Only identical shapes can have equal areas.
Area requires equal perimeters.
options.misconception: links equal area to equal perimeter

options.text: Different dimensions cannot share area.
options.misconception: denies equal areas for different shapes

questions.explanation: A 4 by 4 square has area 16 and an 8 by 2 rectangle has area 16, so they can have equal areas. Options B, C, and D make false claims.

questions.stem: A clinician's note diagram shows rectangle 7 by 9 cm; which expression gives area?

options.text: It adds dimensions instead of multiplying.
The rectangle area equals 7 times 9 square cm.
It squares length incorrectly.
It squares width incorrectly.

questions.explanation: Rectangle area is length times width, so 7 times 9 is correct. Option A adds, C squares length, and D squares width.

questions.learningObjective: Detect an error in unit square area
questions.stem: A clinician's note counts 12 unit squares but reports area 15 for a 3 by 4 rectangle; what error is present?

options.text: It applies triangle factor.
It squares square count.
The correct area is 12 square units total.
It adds dimensions instead of multiplying.

questions.explanation: A 3 by 4 rectangle contains 12 unit squares, so area is 12 square units. Option C states this. Options A, B, and D describe other mistakes.

questions.stem: A clinician's note has parallelogram base 11 cm perpendicular height 4 cm; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Parallelogram area is base times perpendicular height. Eleven times 4 equals 44 square centimeters. The tempting error is using side length.

questions.stem: A clinician's note measures trapezoid bases 7 and 11 cm height 4 cm; find area in square centimeters.
questions.explanation: Trapezoid area is one half times 7 plus 11 times 4, or 36 square centimeters. The tempting error is multiplying bases directly.

questions.explanation: Kite area is one half product of diagonals. One half of 14 times 6 equals 42 square centimeters. The tempting error is omitting one half.

questions.stem: A clinician's note asks why triangle area has factor one half; what is correct?

options.text: It links side count to factor.
It claims height is always doubled.
Because a triangle is half of a parallelogram with same base and height.
It claims the base is excluded from area.

questions.explanation: A triangle with a given base and height occupies half of the corresponding parallelogram, so the one-half factor applies. Options A, B, and D give incorrect reasons.

questions.stem: A clinician's note has an L-shaped region made of two rectangles; which method gives area?

options.text: It subtracts instead of adding.
It multiplies component areas.
It ignores smaller component area.
Add the two non-overlapping rectangle areas.

questions.explanation: Composite area is the sum of non-overlapping component areas, so adding the two rectangles is correct. Options A, B, and C describe errors.

questions.stem: A clinician's note diagram shows a 10 by 10 square with a quarter circle radius 5 cm cut out; which remaining area expression uses pi = 3.14?

options.text: 10 times 10 minus one fourth pi 5 squared.
It adds cutout instead of subtracting.
It adds dimensions and uses full circle.
options.misconception: adds dimensions and uses full circle

options.text: It subtracts full circle not quarter.

questions.explanation: Remaining area is square area minus quarter circle area, so 10 times 10 minus one fourth pi 5 squared is correct. Options B, C, and D describe errors.

questions.learningObjective: Detect an error in equal area claim
questions.stem: A clinician's note claims a 5 by 5 square and a triangle base 10 height 5 have unequal areas; what error is present?

options.text: It accepts incorrect inequality.
The two shapes have equal areas in this case.
It assumes square exceeds triangle.
It assumes triangle exceeds square.

questions.explanation: Square area is 25 and triangle area is one half of 10 times 5, or 25, so they are equal. Option B states this. Options A, C, and D describe other mistakes.

questions.stem: A clinician's note asks why trapezoid area averages the bases; what is correct?

Average base times height gives area.
It incorrectly assumes bases are equal.
It claims the height is doubled incorrectly.

questions.explanation: Trapezoid area is average of bases times height, so average base times height gives area. Options A, C, and D give incorrect reasons.
